source_text:
Τέκνον μου, τοῦ λαλοῦντός σοι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ μνησθήσῃ νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας, τιμήσεις δὲ αὐτὸν ὡς κύριον: ὅθεν γὰρ ἡ κυριότης λαλεῖται, ἐκεῖ κύριός ἐστιν.
ἐκζητήσεις δὲ καθ̓ ἡμέραν τὰ πρόσωπα τῶν ἁγίων, ἵνα ἐπαναπαῇς τοῖς λόγοις αὐτῶν.
οὐ ποθήσεις σχίσμα, εἰρηνεύσεις δὲ μαχομένους: κρινεῖς δικαίως, οὐ λήψῃ πρόσωπον ἐλέγξαι ἐπὶ παραπτώμασιν.
οὐ διψυχήσεις, πότερον ἔσται ἢ οὔ.
Μὴ γίνου πρὸς μὲν τὸ λαβεῖν ἐκτείνων τὰς χεῖρας, πρὸς δὲ τὸ δοῦναι συσπῶν.
ἐὰν ἔχῃς διὰ τῶν χειρῶν σου, δώσεις λύτρωσιν ἁμαρτιῶν σου.
οὐ διστάσεις δοῦναι οὐδὲ διδοὺς γογγύσεις: γνώσῃ γάρ, τίς ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ μισθοῦ καλὸς ἀνταποδότης.
οὐκ ἀποστραφήσῃ τὸν ἐνδεόμενον, συγκοινωνήσεις δὲ πάντα τῷ ἀδελφῷ σοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐρεῖς ἴδια εἶναι: εἰ γὰρ ἐν τῷ ἀθανάτῳ κοινωνοί ἐστε, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ἐν τοῖς θνητοῖς;
Οὐκ ἀρεῖς τὴν χεῖρά σου ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ σου ἢ ἀπὸ τῆς θυγατρός σου, ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ νεότητος διδάξεις τὸν φόβον τοῦ θεοῦ.
οὐκ ἐπιτάξεις δούλῳ σου ἢ παιδίσκῃ, τοῖς ἐπὶ τὸν αὐτὸν θεὸν ἐλπίζουσιν, ἐν πικρίᾳ σου, μήποτε οὐ μὴ φοβηθήσονται τὸν ἐπ’ ἀμφοτέροις θεόν: οὐ γὰρ ἔρχεται κατὰ πρόσωπον καλέσαι, ἀλλ’ ἐφ̓ οὕς τὸ πνεῦμα ἡτοίμασεν.
ὑμεῖς δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι ὑποταγήσεσθε τοῖς κυρίοις ὑμῶν ὡς τύπῳ θεοῦ ἐν αἰσχύνῃ καὶ φόβῳ.
Μισήσεις πᾶσαν ὑπόκρισιν καὶ πᾶν ὃ μὴ ἀρεστὸν τῷ κυρίῳ.
οὐ μὴ ἐγκαταλίπῃς ἐντολὰς κυρίου, φυλάξεις δὲ ἃ παρέλαβες, μήτε προστιθεὶς μήτε ἀφαιρῶν.
ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐξομολογήσῃ τὰ παραπτώματά σου, καὶ οὐ προσελεύσῃ ἐπὶ προσευχήν σου ἐν συνειδήσει πονηρᾷ: αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ὁδὸς τῆς ζωῆς.
thought_title: Honor teachers, seek the saints, and keep the commandments
orientation: The anonymous teacher continues the Way of Life, addressing the hearer as 'my child' with commands about honoring those who speak God's word, seeking the saints, avoiding schism, giving without hesitation, and keeping the Lord's commandments.
pass_a_gloss: My child, you will remember night and day the one who speaks to you the word of God, and you will honor him as Lord; for where the lordship is spoken, there the Lord is. And you will seek out daily the faces of the saints, so that you may rest upon their words. You will not desire schism, but you will make peace between those who fight; you will judge justly, you will not show partiality when rebuking for transgressions. You will not be double-minded whether it will be or not. Do not become one who stretches out the hands toward taking, but draws them in toward giving. If you have something through your hands, you will give a ransom for your sins. You will not hesitate to give, nor will you grumble while giving; for you will know who is the good repayer of the wage. You will not turn away from the one in need, but you will share all things with your brother and you will not say that they are your own; for if you are sharers in the immortal, how much more in the mortal things? You will not take your hand away from your son or from your daughter, but from youth you will teach the fear of God. You will not command your male slave or female slave, who hope in the same God, in your bitterness, lest they should not fear the God who is over both; for he does not come to call according to appearance, but to those whom the Spirit has prepared. But you slaves, be subject to your masters as to a type of God in shame and fear. You will hate all hypocrisy and everything that is not pleasing to the Lord. You will not forsake the commandments of the Lord, but you will guard what you received, neither adding nor taking away. In the assembly you will confess your transgressions, and you will not come to your prayer with an evil conscience; this is the way of life.

choices.term: ὅθεν γὰρ ἡ κυριότης λαλεῖται, ἐκεῖ κύριός ἐστιν
choices.english: for where the lordship is spoken, there the Lord is
choices.why: Keeps the abstract noun κυριότης as 'lordship' to preserve the wordplay with κύριος, and the passive λαλεῖται as 'is spoken' to retain the impersonal force
rejected: for where the Lord's authority is proclaimed, there the Lord is present

choices.english: so that you may rest upon their words
choices.why: ἐπαναπαῇς is a compound of 'rest upon'; the dative τοῖς λόγοις is rendered literally as 'upon their words' to keep the image of leaning on speech
rejected: so that you may find rest in their words

choices.term: οὐ λήψῃ πρόσωπον ἐλέγξαι ἐπὶ παραπτώμασιν
choices.english: you will not show partiality when rebuking for transgressions
choices.why: The idiom λαμβάνειν πρόσωπον means to show favoritism; rendered as 'show partiality' to keep the Semitic idiom visible while remaining English
rejected: you will not accept a face to rebuke

choices.english: whether it will be or not
choices.why: The indirect question with πότερον...ἢ οὔ is kept as a literal either/or construction to preserve the double-minded wavering
rejected: whether something will happen or not

choices.english: as to a type of God
choices.why: τύπος is rendered as 'type' to preserve the theological sense of the master as a visible representation or imprint of God, not merely an example
rejected: as to a model of God
as to an image of God

choices.why: The prepositional phrase is kept literal; αἰσχύνη is 'shame' rather than 'reverence' to preserve the strong word

pass_b_english: My child, remember day and night the one who speaks the word of God to you, and honor him as you honor the Lord, for where the Lord's authority is proclaimed, there the Lord is. Seek out the presence of the holy ones every day, so that you may rest upon their words. Do not desire division, but make peace between those who quarrel. Judge justly, and do not show partiality when rebuking for transgressions. Do not be double-minded, wavering over whether it will be or not.

Do not stretch out your hands to receive and then draw them back when it is time to give. If you have something in your hands, give it as a ransom for your sins. Do not hesitate to give, and do not grumble when you give, for you will know who the good repayer of the wage is. Do not turn away from the one in need, but share everything with your brother, and do not say that anything is your own. For if you are partners in what is immortal, how much more are you partners in what is mortal?

Do not withhold your hand from your son or from your daughter, but from their youth teach them the fear of God. Do not give orders in your bitterness to your male or female slave, who hope in the same God, lest they surely not fear the God who is over you both. For he does not come to call according to outward appearance, but to those whom the Spirit has prepared. And you who are slaves, submit to your masters as to God's pattern, in shame and fear.

Hate all hypocrisy and everything that is not pleasing to the Lord. Do not abandon the commandments of the Lord, but guard what you have received, neither adding to it nor taking away. In the assembly confess your transgressions, and do not approach your prayer with an evil conscience. This is the way of life.

problems.why: Double negative in Greek means 'lest they NOT fear'; English 'cease to fear' loses the emphatic negation and flips to positive fear ceasing.
problems.fix: lest they never come to fear the God who is over you both.

problems.why: Glossary fixes 'ὑποκριταί' as 'hypocrites' but the related abstract noun should follow the same domain; however, the real issue is that 'hypocrisy' is not the glossary term for the related word, and more importantly, the glossary bans 'pretenders' but doesn't directly govern 'ὑπόκρισιν'. Re-reading: the glossary governs 'ὑποκριταί' specifically. This is not a glossary violation. However, checking again: the source has 'ὑπόκρισιν' not 'ὑποκριταί', so no glossary violation. But wait—the instruction says to check if English uses rendering other than brief's fixed glossary. The glossary doesn't cover 'ὑπόκρισιν'. Not a violation. Removing this finding.

edits.old: lest they cease to fear the God who is over you both
edits.new: lest they never come to fear the God who is over you both

fixed: The 'hypocrisy' finding was removed: the glossary governs 'ὑποκριταί' (hypocrites), not the abstract noun 'ὑπόκρισιν', so 'hypocrisy' is not a glossary violation.

problems.quote: as to a type of God
problems.why: 'τύπῳ' here means 'pattern' or 'image' (likeness), not 'type' in the modern sense. Slaves should see masters as God's representative/pattern.
problems.fix: as to God's pattern, or as representing God

problems.quote: lest they never come to fear
problems.why: Double negative οὐ μὴ + subjunctive is emphatic negation 'they will surely not fear,' not 'lest they never come to fear.' The Greek warns against causing them NOT to fear God.
problems.fix: lest they cease to fear, or surely not fear, the God who is over you both
problems.ruling: μήποτε οὐ μὴ φοβηθήσονται: οὐ μὴ = emphatic negation, 'lest they not fear'; 'never come to fear' misreads

edits.old: as to a type of God
lest they never come to fear the God who is over you both
edits.new: lest they surely not fear the God who is over you both

problems.quote: where the lordship is spoken, there the Lord is
problems.why: 'lordship is spoken' is not idiomatic English; meaning is unclear.
problems.fix: Render as 'where the lordship of God is proclaimed' or 'where the word of the Lord is spoken.'

edits.old: for where the lordship is spoken, there the Lord is.
edits.new: for where the Lord's authority is proclaimed, there the Lord is.

last_rejected.why: Brief glossary maps ὑποκριταί/ὑπόκρισιν to 'hypocrites'; noun form should match.
last_rejected.fix: Hate every hypocrite and everything that is not pleasing to the Lord.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπόκρισιν is 'hypocrisy'; glossary mapping of related forms is normal lexicographic practice, not broken.
